source_name: MNB – Pénzfeldolgozási tevékenység engedélyezése (register of licensed cash-processing organisations)
why_relevant: Regulator page hosting the official downloadable list of organisations licensed by MNB to perform cash processing (pénzfeldolgozás). This is the authoritative census of the HU cash-cycle service provider population and the entry point for actor mapping of CIT/cash-logistics firms.

source_name: MNB – Bankjegy és érme / Az MNB készpénzes tevékenysége
why_relevant: Central bank hub for currency issuance, banknote/coin production, cash-cycle rules and the banknote-and-coin regulation (bankjegy- és érmerendelet) that governs cash recirculation, machine testing and CIT obligations.

source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabálytár / Jogtár – 2025. évi XVIII. törvény az automata bankjegykiadó gépek telepítéséről ("ATM Act")
why_relevant: The legal ATM mandate itself: obliges payment service providers to install ATMs in every settlement on a phased schedule (>1000 inhabitants by end-2025, 500-1000 by end-2026) with MNB fines of HUF 2m-200m. Baseline for compliance-driven ATM deployment tracking.

source_name: MNB decree setting minimum ATM counts per credit institution (5/2025. (IV.17.) MNB rendelet family, on njt.hu)
why_relevant: Secondary regulation quantifying per-bank ATM operating obligations by card-portfolio band (reported thresholds e.g. min. 169 ATMs for smaller issuers, 1686 for the largest). Directly drives ATM procurement/consolidation volumes.

source_name: Pénzjegynyomda Zrt. (Hungarian Banknote Printing Company) corporate site & published financial statements
why_relevant: MNB-owned banknote printer; its published standalone annual report gives revenue (reported net revenue HUF 21.37bn for 2024) and capacity/segment commentary — a rare quantitative window on the physical banknote supply chain.

source_name: e-beszámoló (Ministry of Justice company financial statements portal)
why_relevant: Mandatory filing portal where every HU cash-logistics/CIT firm (G4S Készpénzlogisztikai, Criterion, Prompt Security, Risec, Pénzjegynyomda, ATM deployers) files audited accounts — the only way to size the CIT market by revenue and headcount.

source_name: Nemzeti Cégtár / OPTEN company registry data
why_relevant: Commercial company-registry aggregators giving ownership, TEÁOR activity codes, revenue and headcount for cash-logistics and ATM-operating entities; useful to enumerate the sector by activity code and detect ownership changes/consolidation.

source_name: G4S Magyarország – Készpénzmenedzsment (cash management services)
why_relevant: Major HU CIT/cash-processing operator (G4S Készpénzlogisztikai Kft.), historically replenishing ATMs for OTP and foreign-owned banks and processing retail cash. Service pages reveal capability set, coverage and MNB-accredited equipment claims.

source_name: CRITERION Készpénzlogisztikai Kft.
why_relevant: Long-established HU CIT firm (since 1992) claiming market leadership; offers cash transport, cash/valuables processing, ATM operation and vaulting — a core actor for cash-cycle capacity and pricing intelligence.

source_name: Prompt Security Zrt. (cash logistics, cash processing, ATM operation)
why_relevant: HU cash-logistics/security firm stating ~25 years of value transport, cash processing, vaulting and automat (ATM) operation for financial and retail clients — relevant to ATM-as-a-service and outsourcing supply in HU.

source_name: Risec – Pénz- és értékszállítás, pénzfeldolgozás
why_relevant: One of the oldest HU CIT operators (claims 1989 start); adds to the actor map of the domestic cash-transport market and its fragmentation.

source_name: SecuriFocus – Pénzszállítás cégadatbázis (security-industry company directory)
why_relevant: Sector directory listing HU cash-transport companies — a cheap snowballing source to enumerate smaller regional CIT operators not visible in national press.

source_name: Euronet Magyarország – bank-independent ATM network (euronetatms.hu)
why_relevant: Largest bank-independent ATM deployer in HU (self-reported ~600 ATMs, expansion under a community/village ATM programme). Its HU press releases disclose ATM counts, FX-withdrawal features and rollout plans relevant to the ATM mandate.

source_name: Kormany.hu – government communications on the universal ATM / free cash withdrawal obligation
why_relevant: Policy-owner announcements framing the ATM mandate and the HUF 150k free-withdrawal obligation; often the first place deployment targets and deadlines are quantified.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Értesítő / EKR – public procurement notices for cash transport and ATM operation
why_relevant: State-owned banks, Magyar Posta, MNB and municipalities tender CIT, cash-processing and ATM operation contracts here; award notices disclose incumbents, contract values and volumes — the hardest pricing evidence available in this cell.

source_name: Pénzcentrum / Bank360 / FinTechZone – HU fintech-banking trade press on ATM network restructuring
why_relevant: Consistently cover ATM mandate implementation, per-bank minimum ATM counts, fee changes and network consolidation, often quoting MNB officials and unpublished bank data.

source_name: G7.hu – investigative reporting on ownership of Hungary's cash-handling infrastructure
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: documents ownership changes and consolidation among HU CIT/cash-processing firms (G4S Készpénzlogisztikai, TrezEx ex-Brink's/Securitas) and their bank/retail client bases — information not published by the firms themselves.

source_name: ATM Marketplace (Networld Media) – ATM-as-a-Service and vendor landscape coverage
why_relevant: Trade press tracking ATMaaS, cash recyclers, and the NCR Atleos / Diebold Nixdorf managed-services propositions that HU banks buy when outsourcing ATM estates under the mandate.

source_name: Dunai Gépgyártó / DG Zrt. (dgezrt.hu) – pénz- és értékszállítás service line
why_relevant: Additional HU operator offering money and valuables transport; useful for completing the long tail of the CIT actor map beyond the top three firms.

source_name: MNB – Módszertani útmutató a készpénzforgalmazásról (cash handling methodology guide)
why_relevant: Operational rulebook for cash recirculation, banknote authentication machine testing and reporting duties imposed on banks and cash processors — defines what compliance data CIT firms and ATM operators must generate.

source_name: Magyar Közlöny (Hungarian Official Gazette) – official issue archive
why_relevant: Primary publication venue for every Hungarian act and government/MNB decree; the authoritative first appearance of cash-acceptance duties, free-ATM-withdrawal limits, transaction levy rates and payment-related decrees, with exact dates and numeric thresholds.

source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabálytár (National Legislation Database, njt.hu)
why_relevant: Consolidated, time-versioned texts of Hungarian law; lets you track how quantitative thresholds (levy rates, caps, free-withdrawal amounts) changed over time rather than only the latest version.

source_name: Act CXVI of 2012 on the Financial Transaction Levy (2012. évi CXVI. törvény a pénzügyi tranzakciós illetékről) – Nemzeti Jogszabálytár entry
why_relevant: The core statute defining the levy base and rates per transaction type (transfers, card purchases, cash withdrawal, currency exchange, e-money since 2025-07-20, securities since 2022-08-01); the rate/cap structure is the key to converting levy revenue into implied payment volumes.

source_name: NAV információs füzet 44. – A pénzügyi tranzakciós illeték (annual tax-authority guidance leaflet series)
why_relevant: Yearly authoritative restatement of levy scope, rates, caps, exemptions and filing form numbers (e.g. 2593); the cleanest machine-readable narrative of which payment instruments are taxed at what rate in each year.

source_name: NAV közérdekű adatok / adatbázisok (tax authority public-data and database hub)
why_relevant: Entry point to NAV's statutory publication lists and datasets; the route to levy-revenue and filing-aggregate data and to formal FOI (közérdekű adatigénylés) requests for payment-levy breakdowns not published proactively.

source_name: NAV Pénzügyi és Elemzési Intézet – Statisztikai adatok (pei.nav.gov.hu)
why_relevant: NAV's analytical arm publishing tax statistics; a likely home for time series of transaction-levy receipts, which proxy taxed payment turnover.

source_name: Országgyűlés – irományok (Parliament bill and explanatory-memorandum repository)
why_relevant: Bill texts and general/detailed reasoning (indokolás) for tax packages routinely state expected fiscal yield of transaction-levy changes and the payment-volume assumptions behind them — quantitative intelligence not present in the final gazette text.
